summary: 2 HIGH findings. (1) Privacy policy still uses 'Powderizer' (customer-visible) where all other surfaces say 'Custom Powder' — missed in fiction sweep. (2) README Admin Inventory example self-contradicts: text correctly says 'Use a variant SKU, not a product ID' but body uses deprecated `productId` (string '49') while current route schema requires `variantId` (integer). No critical money/inventory/order/auth defects found. Copy, help, nav, six-category facts, and fiction sweep otherwise complete. No 'Reverse Process', 'trading', 'auctions', 'impossible', 'questionable', 'Powdered Water', 'Chaos Mix', or 'daily recipe' in customer-visible surfaces. High-level plan direction clean. Disabled controls have standard opacity treatment; no unexplained dead controls. Allergen-filter/localization scope leak absent.

findings.claim: Privacy policy uses 'Powderizer' instead of 'Custom Powder' — missed in fiction sweep
findings.trace: S1 fiction sweep renamed all customer-visible 'Powderizer' -> 'Custom Powder' (nav, hero, FAQ, README, help articles). The privacy policy was missed. User navigating /policies/privacy sees 'bounded Powderizer history in local storage' (L38) and 'Powderizer history already stored in a browser' (L57) — same feature rendered as 'Custom Powder' everywhere else. Inconsistent frontend-backend naming in customer-visible policy text.
findings.fix: Replace 'Powderizer history' with 'Custom Powder history' (or 'Custom Powder blend history') in both occurrences in policyArticles.ts.

findings.claim: README Admin Inventory example uses deprecated `productId` field; route requires `variantId`
findings.trace: S1 added text 'Use a variant SKU, not a product ID' (L194) but left body `"productId": "49"`. Route schema `InventoryReceiptBody` defines `variantId: Type.Integer({ minimum: 1 })` (packages/contracts/src/inventory.ts:4-11); the admin inventory POST handler reads `request.body.variantId` only (apps/api/src/routes/adminInventory.ts:62). `productId` is `additionalProperties: false`-rejected. User following README example gets a 400 validation error. Also 'SKU' (string like 'SN-WHEY-1000') is misleading — the actual `variantId` is a database integer ID.
findings.fix: Replace body `"productId": "49"` with `"variantId": 1` and change text from 'Use a variant SKU, not a product ID:' to 'Use a numeric variant ID (integer, not SKU string):' or similar correct guidance.
